issue_context.title: Preset modes are not identified/set in Honeywell Total Connect Comfort (US)
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When I check the state of my device it does not show the preset mode that it is in. See pic.

It asks during setup what my upper/lower limits are for Away/Vacation mode, but it doesn't use them for anything as it can't even identify the mode it is in.

The modes are clearly being pulled, but you can't use a service to set them AND it is not pulling the current one it is set for.

This, also, prevents me from using HA for Home/Away type of functions.

N/A

It appears you can not set a hold when in "auto" mode - only when in HEAT or COOL modes. 
Maybe it should allow this?  Maybe we need to set heat and cool set points, but I'm not sure which "set_hold_(heat/cool)" we would set in "auto" mode.

``> It appears you can not set a hold when in "auto" mode - only when in HEAT or COOL modes. Maybe it should allow this? Maybe we need to set heat and cool set points, but I'm not sure which "set_hold_(heat/cool)" we would set in "auto" mode.

I can set mine to hold with a temp for hot and cold.  Below is my automation to do so.

`alias: Heating/Cooling-Set Temp M-F 0600-0830
description: ""
trigger:
  - platform: time
    at: "06:00:00"
condition:
  - after: "06:00:00"
    before: "08:30:00"
    condition: time
    weekday:
      - mon
      - tue
      - wed
      - thu
      - fri
action:
  - data:
      target_temp_high: 75
      target_temp_low: 70
    service: climate.set_temperature
    target:
      entity_id: climate.home
mode: restart
`

My issue is that I lose out on some of the inherit functions of my thermostat.  I'd prefer to use the standard thermostat schedule but allow it to go to a hold when everyone leaves with a hot/cold and then resume the normal schedule when someone returns.

The main feature I am missing is the ability to use recovery mode where the thermostat looks at the schedule it has programmed and basically analyzed the data, and starts heating or cooling before a schedule change.  E.g. I want it to heat/cool to 70/75 when I return from work, then it will start before that time to make sure it is there when I get home.

If I use all automation, the thermostat becomes dumb and just changes when I tell it to.  Where I live we have wild temperature swings so the use of the recovery mode and the data the thermostat uses makes it learn over time.

So I'd like to use the built in schedule for that, but use HA to set heat/cool set points when I set it to Away, but right now I can't call that service.

I may be misunderstanding: `AttributeError: 'HoneywellUSThermostat' object has no attribute '_auto_away_temp'` can only happen when mode = "auto".  If you attempt to call that service with mode "auto" it fails because there are only _cool_away_temp and _heat_away_temp attributes.  
I can make the error go away (and will), but it still would not set <mode>_away_temp because I'm not sure what the thermostat wants.
We could try to set both heat and cool temps when it's in auto mode, but I don't know which hold to set - heat or cool (maybe both?).

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/honeywell/climate.py#L303-L309

OK I understand what you are saying now.  My apologies.

The weird part is when I load the Honeywell integration it asks for my away heat temp and my away cool temp so I thought calling the service would handle that.

Either way, yeah my thermostat at least always asks for an upper (cool) and lower (heat) the way I have mine setup.

There is another mode where you can set a single temp for everything, but I never use it.
